Specification: TLAPS proof library of theorems and operators on sequences. Defines Cons, InsertAt, RemoveAt, Front, Last, Reverse, IsPrefix, IsStrictPrefix, IsSuffix, IsStrictSuffix, StrictPrefixesDetermineDef, StrictSuffixesDetermineDef, TailInductiveDefHypothesis/Conclusion, FrontInductiveDefHypothesis/Conclusion and proves a comprehensive collection of theorems and lemmas covering element membership, length, equality, concatenation, subsequences, head/tail, append, cons, insertion/removal, front/last, reverse, prefix/suffix orderings (incl. well-foundedness) and prefix/suffix-recursive function definitions.
IfThenElse: IF j=i THEN e ELSE seq[j]
IF i <= Len(s1) THEN s1[i] ELSE s2[i - Len(s1)]
IF seq = <<>> THEN elt ELSE Head(seq)
IF seq = <<>> THEN <<>> ELSE Append(Tail(seq), elt)
IF j<i THEN seq[j] ELSE IF j=i THEN elt ELSE seq[j-1]
IF j<i THEN seq[j] ELSE seq[j+1]
IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Tail(s)], s)
IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[Tail(s)], s)
IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Front(s)], s)
IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[Front(s)], s)
FunctionConstructor: [s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Tail(s)], s)]
[s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[Tail(s)], s)]
[s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Front(s)], s)]
[s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[Front(s)], s)]
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE g : g = [s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Tail(s)], s)]
CHOOSE g : g = [s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Front(s)], s)]
AssumeProveBlocks: ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW n \in 1..Len(seq) PROVE seq[n] \in S
ASSUME NEW S PROVE /\ << >> \in Seq(S) /\ \A seq \in Seq(S) : (seq = << >>) <=> (Len(seq) = 0)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ Len(seq) \in Nat /\ seq \in [1..Len(seq) -> S] /\ DOMAIN seq = 1 .. Len(seq)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW i \in 1 .. Len(seq), NEW e \in S PROVE /\ [seq EXCEPT ![i] = e] \in Seq(S) /\ Len([seq EXCEPT ![i] = e]) = Len(seq) /\ \A j \in 1 .. Len(seq) : [seq EXCEPT ![i] = e][j] = IF j=i THEN e ELSE seq[j]
ASSUME NEW n \in Nat, NEW e(_), NEW S, \A i \in 1..n : e(i) \in S PROVE [i \in 1..n |-> e(i)] \in Seq(S)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), Len(s) = Len(t), \A i \in 1 .. Len(s) : s[i] = t[i] PROVE s = t

ASSUME NEW S, NEW s1 \in Seq(S), NEW s2 \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ s1 \o s2 \in Seq(S) /\ Len(s1 \o s2) = Len(s1) + Len(s2) /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(s1) + Len(s2) : (s1 \o s2)[i] = IF i <= Len(s1) THEN s1[i] ELSE s2[i - Len(s1)]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ seq \o << >> = seq /\ << >> \o seq = seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s1 \in Seq(S), NEW s2 \in Seq(S), NEW s3 \in Seq(S) PROVE (s1 \o s2) \o s3 = s1 \o (s2 \o s3)
ASSUME NEW S PROVE concat simplifications: cancellation laws on \o for sequences
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(s)+1, NEW n \in m-1 .. Len(s) PROVE /\ SubSeq(s,m,n) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(SubSeq(s, m, n)) = n-m+1 /\ \A i \in 1 .. n-m+1 : SubSeq(s,m,n)[i] = s[m+i-1]
ASSUME NEW s, NEW m \in Int, NEW n \in Int, n < m PROVE SubSeq(s,m,n) = << >>
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE /\ Head(seq) \in S /\ Tail(seq) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(Tail(seq)) = Len(seq)-1 /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(Tail(seq)) : Tail(seq)[i] = seq[i+1]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE Tail(seq) = SubSeq(seq, 2, Len(seq))
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW n \in 0 .. Len(seq) PROVE SubSeq(seq, 1, n) = Restrict(seq, 1 .. n)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(seq), NEW n \in m .. Len(seq) PROVE /\ Head(SubSeq(seq,m,n)) = seq[m] /\ Tail(SubSeq(seq,m,n)) = SubSeq(seq, m+1, n)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(seq), NEW n \in m .. Len(seq) PROVE SubSeq(seq, m, n) = << seq[m] >> \o SubSeq(seq, m+1, n)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(seq), NEW n \in m .. Len(seq) PROVE SubSeq(seq, m, n) = SubSeq(seq, m, n-1) \o << seq[n] >>
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(s)+1, NEW n \in m-1 .. Len(s), NEW i \in 1 .. n-m+2, NEW j \in i-1 .. n-m+1 PROVE SubSeq( SubSeq(s,m,n), i, j ) = SubSeq(s, m+i-1, m+j-1)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE SubSeq(seq, 1, Len(seq)) = seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(seq)+1, NEW k \in m-1 .. Len(seq), NEW n \in k .. Len(seq) PROVE SubSeq(seq, m, k) \o SubSeq(seq, k+1, n) = SubSeq(seq, m, n)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW elt \in S PROVE /\ Append(seq, elt) \in Seq(S) /\ Append(seq, elt) # << >> /\ Len(Append(seq, elt)) = Len(seq)+1 /\ \A i \in 1.. Len(seq) : Append(seq, elt)[i] = seq[i] /\ Append(seq, elt)[Len(seq)+1] = elt
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW elt \in S PROVE Append(seq, elt) = seq \o <<elt>>
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW elt PROVE /\ Head(Append(seq, elt)) = IF seq = <<>> THEN elt ELSE Head(seq) /\ Tail(Append(seq, elt)) = IF seq = <<>> THEN <<>> ELSE Append(Tail(seq), elt)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW elt \in S PROVE /\ Cons(elt, seq) \in Seq(S) /\ Cons(elt, seq) # <<>> /\ Len(Cons(elt, seq)) = Len(seq)+1 /\ Head(Cons(elt, seq)) = elt /\ Tail(Cons(elt, seq)) = seq /\ Cons(elt, seq)[1] = elt /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(seq) : Cons(elt, seq)[i+1] = seq[i]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE Cons(Head(seq), Tail(seq)) = seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW x \in S, NEW y \in S PROVE Cons(x, Append(seq, y)) = Append(Cons(x,seq), y)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW f \in S, NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE Cons(e,s) = Cons(f,t) <=> e = f /\ s = t

ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW i \in 1 .. Len(seq)+1, NEW elt \in S PROVE /\ InsertAt(seq,i,elt) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(InsertAt(seq,i,elt)) = Len(seq)+1 /\ \A j \in 1 .. Len(seq)+1 : InsertAt(seq,i,elt)[j] = IF j<i THEN seq[j] ELSE IF j=i THEN elt ELSE seq[j-1]

ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW i \in 1..Len(seq) PROVE /\ RemoveAt(seq,i) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(RemoveAt(seq,i)) = Len(seq) - 1 /\ \A j \in 1 .. Len(seq)-1 : RemoveAt(seq,i)[j] = IF j<i THEN seq[j] ELSE seq[j+1]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ Front(seq) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(Front(seq)) = IF seq = << >> THEN 0 ELSE Len(seq)-1 /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(seq)-1 : Front(seq)[i] = seq[i]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE /\ Last(seq) \in S /\ Append(Front(seq), Last(seq)) = seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1 .. Len(seq), NEW n \in m .. Len(seq) PROVE /\ Front(SubSeq(seq,m,n)) = SubSeq(seq, m, n-1) /\ Last(SubSeq(seq,m,n)) = seq[n]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW e \in S PROVE /\ Front(Append(seq, e)) = seq /\ Last(Append(seq, e)) = e
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW f \in S, NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE Append(s,e) = Append(t,f) <=> s = t /\ e = f
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE \E s \in Seq(S), elt \in S : seq = Append(s, elt)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ Reverse(seq) \in Seq(S) /\ Len(Reverse(seq)) = Len(seq) /\ Reverse(Reverse(seq)) = seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), Reverse(s) = Reverse(t) PROVE s = t
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), Reverse(seq) = <<>> PROVE seq = <<>>
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s1 \in Seq(S), NEW s2 \in Seq(S) PROVE Reverse(s1 \o s2) = Reverse(s2) \o Reverse(s1)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW e \in S PROVE Reverse(Append(seq,e)) = Cons(e, Reverse(seq))
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW e \in S PROVE Reverse(Cons(e,seq)) = Append(Reverse(seq), e)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), NEW m \in 1..Len(seq), NEW n \in 1..Len(seq) PROVE Reverse(SubSeq(seq, m , n)) = SubSeq(Reverse(seq), Len(seq)-n+1, Len(seq)-m+1)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), Reverse(seq) = seq PROVE Reverse(seq \o seq) = seq \o seq
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE Last(seq) = Head(Reverse(seq))
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S), seq # << >> PROVE Reverse(Front(seq)) = Tail(Reverse(seq))
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW S, P(<< >>), \A s \in Seq(S), e \in S : P(s) => P(Append(s,e)) PROVE \A seq \in Seq(S) : P(seq)
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW S, P(<< >>), \A s \in Seq(S), e \in S : P(s) => P(Cons(e,s)) PROVE \A seq \in Seq(S) : P(seq)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE Range(seq) \in SUBSET S
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE Range(seq) = { seq[i] : i \in 1 .. Len(seq) }
ASSUME NEW S, NEW seq \in Seq(S) PROVE Range(Reverse(seq)) = Range(seq)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s1 \in Seq(S), NEW s2 \in Seq(S) PROVE Range(s1 \o s2) = Range(s1) \cup Range(s2)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ IsPrefix(s,t) <=> \E u \in Seq(S) : t = s \o u /\ IsPrefix(s,t) <=> Len(s) <= Len(t) /\ s = SubSeq(t, 1, Len(s)) /\ IsPrefix(s,t) <=> Len(s) <= Len(t) /\ s = Restrict(t, DOMAIN s)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW i \in 1 .. Len(s), IsPrefix(s,t) PROVE s[i] = t[i]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ IsPrefix(<<>>, s) /\ IsPrefix(s, <<>>) <=> s = <<>> /\ IsStrictPrefix(<<>>, s) <=> s # <<>> /\ ~ IsStrictPrefix(s, <<>>)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE IsPrefix(s, s \o t)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW e \in S PROVE IsPrefix(s, Append(s,e))
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ IsPrefix(Front(s), s) /\ s # <<>> => IsStrictPrefix(Front(s), s)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), IsPrefix(s,t) PROVE Range(s) \subseteq Range(t)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), IsPrefix(s,t), NEW Op(_) PROVE IsPrefix([i \in DOMAIN s |-> Op(s[i])], [i \in DOMAIN t |-> Op(t[i])])
ASSUME NEW S PROVE prefix is a partial order on Seq(S)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S), IsPrefix(s \o t, u) PROVE IsPrefix(s, u)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S) PROVE IsPrefix(s \o t, s \o u) <=> IsPrefix(t, u)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE IsPrefix(Cons(e,s), Cons(e,t)) <=> IsPrefix(s,t)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S), IsPrefix(Cons(e,s), u) PROVE /\ e = Head(u) /\ IsPrefix(s, Tail(u))
ASSUME NEW S PROVE IsStrictPrefix is a strict partial order
ASSUME NEW S PROVE IsWellFoundedOn(OpToRel(IsStrictPrefix, Seq(S)), Seq(S))
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW S, \A t \in Seq(S) : (\A s \in Seq(S) : IsStrictPrefix(s,t) => P(s)) => P(t) PROVE \A s \in Seq(S) : P(s)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE three IsSuffix characterisations
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW i \in 1 .. Len(s), IsSuffix(s,t) PROVE s[i] = t[Len(t) - Len(s) + i]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ IsSuffix(<<>>, s) /\ IsSuffix(s, <<>>) <=> s = <<>> /\ IsStrictSuffix(<<>>, s) <=> s # <<>> /\ ~ IsStrictSuffix(s, <<>>)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE IsSuffix(s, t \o s)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW e \in S PROVE IsStrictSuffix(s, Cons(e,s))
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S) PROVE /\ IsSuffix(Tail(s), s) /\ s # <<>> => IsStrictSuffix(Tail(s), s)
ASSUME NEW S PROVE IsSuffix partial order on Seq(S)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S), IsSuffix(s \o t, u) PROVE IsSuffix(t, u)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S) PROVE IsSuffix(s \o t, u \o t) <=> IsSuffix(s, u)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW t \in Seq(S) PROVE IsSuffix(Append(s,e), Append(t,e)) <=> IsSuffix(s,t)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW e \in S, NEW s \in Seq(S), NEW u \in Seq(S), IsSuffix(Append(s,e), u) PROVE /\ e = Last(u) /\ IsSuffix(s, Front(u))
ASSUME NEW S PROVE IsStrictSuffix strict partial order on Seq(S)
ASSUME NEW S PROVE IsWellFoundedOn(OpToRel(IsStrictSuffix, Seq(S)), Seq(S))
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW S, \A t \in Seq(S) : (\A s \in Seq(S) : IsStrictSuffix(s,t) => P(s)) => P(t) PROVE \A s \in Seq(S) : P(s)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), StrictPrefixesDetermineDef(S, Def) PROVE WFDefOn(OpToRel(IsStrictPrefix, Seq(S)), Seq(S), Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), StrictPrefixesDetermineDef(S, Def) PROVE WFInductiveUnique(Seq(S), Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, StrictPrefixesDetermineDef(S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, Seq(S), Def) PROVE WFInductiveDefines(f, Seq(S), Def)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW T, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, T # {}, StrictPrefixesDetermineDef(S, Def), WFInductiveDefines(f, Seq(S), Def), \A g \in [Seq(S) -> T], s \in Seq(S) : Def(g,s) \in T PROVE f \in [Seq(S) -> T]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), StrictSuffixesDetermineDef(S, Def) PROVE WFDefOn(OpToRel(IsStrictSuffix, Seq(S)), Seq(S), Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), StrictSuffixesDetermineDef(S, Def) PROVE WFInductiveUnique(Seq(S), Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, StrictSuffixesDetermineDef(S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, Seq(S), Def) PROVE WFInductiveDefines(f, Seq(S), Def)

ASSUME NEW S, NEW T, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, T # {}, StrictSuffixesDetermineDef(S, Def), WFInductiveDefines(f, Seq(S), Def), \A g \in [Seq(S) -> T], s \in Seq(S) : Def(g,s) \in T PROVE f \in [Seq(S) -> T]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW f0, TailInductiveDefHypothesis(f, S, f0, Def) PROVE TailInductiveDefConclusion(f, S, f0, Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW f0, NEW T, TailInductiveDefConclusion(f, S, f0, Def), f0 \in T, \A v \in T, s \in Seq(S) : s # <<>> => Def(v,s) \in T PROVE f \in [Seq(S) -> T]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW f0, FrontInductiveDefHypothesis(f, S, f0, Def) PROVE FrontInductiveDefConclusion(f, S, f0, Def)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW Def(_,_), NEW f, NEW f0, NEW T, FrontInductiveDefConclusion(f, S, f0, Def), f0 \in T, \A v \in T, s \in Seq(S) : s # <<>> => Def(v,s) \in T PROVE f \in [Seq(S) -> T]
FunctionConstructor_ByDomain: [s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(g[Tail(s)], s)]
[s \in Seq(S) |-> IF s = <<>> THEN f0 ELSE Def(f[Tail(s)], s)]

DivisionNotes: Predicate-style operators (IsPrefix, IsStrictPrefix, IsSuffix, IsStrictSuffix, StrictPrefixesDetermineDef, StrictSuffixesDetermineDef, TailInductiveDefHypothesis/Conclusion, FrontInductiveDefHypothesis/Conclusion) are classified as StatePredicate.
Sequence-construction operators (Cons, InsertAt, RemoveAt, Front, Last, Reverse) are classified as ValueDef.
Module is a pure proof library: no Init/Spec/Next, no temporal operators -> TemporalNesting=false, OperatorDefNames_Init=[], TemporalProperty=[].
FunctionConstructor split: forms [x \in S |-> e] go to ByDomain; arrow-typed [S -> T] forms go to SetType.
VerificationTools=TLAPS: theorems are TLAPS-proved (proofs in SequenceTheorems_proofs).
